plan.title: Client Retention, Appreciation, and Acquisition Plan

principle: Redtail is the system of record and Zocks feeds it. If it is not in Redtail, it did not happen. This section holds the experience program and makes its materials. It does not hold client records, so nothing typed here is saved, and every gift, card, event and touch is logged in Redtail.

signatures.name: Speed
signatures.detail: Every request acknowledged within 4 business hours, resolved or updated within 2 business days.

signatures.name: Memory
signatures.detail: No client repeats themselves. The Redtail profile and Zocks notes brief whoever picks up the call.

signatures.name: Anticipation
signatures.detail: Contact before the client asks: key dates, milestones, the pre-filing window for draft returns, year end, business inflection points.

signatures.name: Access
signatures.detail: A named human with a direct line: Becky for Tier 1, Maddie for service in Tiers 1 to 3.

signatures.name: Belonging
signatures.detail: The Owner Roundtable: six to eight Tier 1 owners, twice a year, opt in, no sales content, compliance cleared. Peer access is what an owner cannot buy elsewhere.

tiers.name: VIP Anchor Families
tiers.who: Retainer families on the full Seven Pillars
tiers.model: Quarterly 90-day sprint, monthly pulse, direct access, milestone program, multigenerational track, Owner Roundtable

tiers.name: Building Owners
tiers.who: Owners in or entering the $6,000 Complete Assessment, or with a defined exit or growth window and no retainer
tiers.criteria: Assessment signed or in active pipeline
tiers.model: Onboarding workflow, monthly contact, conversion conversation at day 90

tiers.name: Core Clients
tiers.who: Active advisory or in-force insurance clients without a retainer
tiers.criteria: Active account or policy, no retainer
tiers.model: Annual review, two scheduled touches, milestone cards, annual client event

tiers.name: Dormant
tiers.who: No meaningful contact in 18 or more months and no active service need
tiers.model: One 60-day reactivation sequence, then a closing letter. No experience spend.

capacity: Twenty Tier 1 families on quarterly sprints is 80 sessions a year. At 4.5 hours each, that is 360 hours, about 6.9 hours a week of Becky's calendar.
Events and family sessions add about 172 hours, for 532 hours a year, about 10.2 hours a week, before onboarding, annual reviews and Tier 3.
Each new Tier 1 family adds 18 hours a year. The planning seat is the capacity valve.
Every target is a proposal until the Phase 0 baseline is pulled from Redtail.

rollout.gate: Maddie runs a test household through every workflow.

rollout.work: Lock the Q1 sprint calendar, start the monthly pulse, send the two-question Net Promoter survey, begin heir identification with parent consent.
rollout.gate: Every Tier 1 household has a next sprint date in Redtail.

rollout.work: Referral workflow live, first Owner Roundtable invitations (compliance cleared), first family session scheduled, first metrics report on February 5.
rollout.gate: Baseline report reviewed; decide whether to extend the Tier 3 touches.

generations.why: Heirs are the largest unprotected retention risk in a family practice, because the relationship sits with the parent. The track builds a direct relationship with each generation before a transfer, not after, so that when the transfer comes the next generation already knows the team, the plan and the reasons behind it.

stages.experience: Pillars 6 and 7 built into every sprint: transition, legacy and estate decisions. Parents approve in writing which heirs are invited and what is shared.
One introductory meeting a year; financial education on their terms; Redtail record created with parent consent.
Annual meeting; successor readiness check tied to the exit plan; a seat at the annual family session.
One a year per household: values and vision refresh, decision rights, how the family talks about money. Becky facilitates; the family's attorney and CPA join through the client.

stages.who: The next generation, after a transfer
stages.experience: Extension, for approval: the heir is invited to engage under their own agreement, with a team they already know. Nothing about the parents' plan is carried over without written consent.

boundaries: Heirs are not clients until they engage under their own agreement.
No parent information is shared with an heir without the parent's written consent.
Minors receive no advisory contact, and no cards are addressed to minors.
The program coordinates and routes to licensed professionals. It does not direct them or draft legal documents.
A child's birth date is recorded only with the parent's consent, and only so the card to the parents can acknowledge it.

materials.name: Parent consent request
materials.note: A request for consent, not a legal document. Routes through compliance before first use.
materials.body:
Dear {{first}},

As part of the planning we are doing together, you have mentioned wanting {{heir}} to understand more about how your family's plan works. Before I contact {{heir}}, I would like your written direction on two things.

First, may I invite {{heir}} to an introductory conversation with me. It is a get-acquainted meeting about {{heir}}'s own questions and goals, not a review of your plan.

Second, what, if anything, may I share with {{heir}} about your plan. You may choose nothing at all, general principles only, or specific items you list. Whatever you decide, I will share nothing beyond it, and you may change your answer at any time.

Please reply with your choices, or we can talk them through at our next meeting.

With warm regards,
{{advisor}}

materials.name: First meeting with an adult heir
materials.note: A conversation guide for Becky. The meeting belongs to the heir.
materials.body:
Purpose: get to know {{heir}} on their own terms, and be the person they would call with a money question.

Before the meeting
- Confirm the parent's written consent and exactly what may be shared. When in doubt, share nothing.
- No meeting with anyone under 18.

Open with their world
- What are you working on right now, and what is next.
- What do you wish someone had explained to you about money.
- Who do you go to with financial questions today.

Offer education they choose (pick one or two, never all)
- Your first paycheck: benefits elections, the 401(k) match, and what to do first.
- Credit and debt: how a score works and how to build one deliberately.
- Your first investments: what a diversified account is and what it costs.
- The family business: what ownership, a buy-sell and a board actually mean.
- How your family makes decisions about money, and where you fit.

Close
- Agree one thing they will do in the next 30 days.
- Tell them how to reach you directly.
- Log the meeting in Redtail on the heir's linked record the same day.

Never
- Discuss the parents' plan, balances or intentions beyond what was consented in writing.
- Recommend a product.

materials.name: Successor readiness check
materials.when: Stewardship stage, tied to the exit plan
materials.note: Questions for a successor aged 30 or older. Readiness is about the person and the role, not about the balance sheet.
materials.body:
Role
- What role do you want in the company in five years, and what role do your parents expect you to have.
- Who in the company would you report to today, and who would report to you.

Preparation
- What decisions have you already made on your own in the business.
- What would you need to learn, and from whom, to run it.

Ownership
- Do you understand how ownership would pass to you: gift, sale, trust or buy-sell.
- Have you read the buy-sell agreement, and do you know what it says happens if a parent dies or becomes disabled.

Family
- If you are not the only heir, how will fairness be handled between those who work in the business and those who do not.
- Who decides when the family disagrees.

Next step
- One action before the next family session, logged in Redtail.

materials.name: Annual family session agenda
materials.when: Once a year per household, January to June
materials.note: Three hours, Pillars 1, 6 and 7. Becky facilitates; the family's attorney and CPA join through the client.
materials.body:
Before: parents approve the invitation list and what is shared, in writing. Pre-read sent five business days ahead: last year's values statement and the open decisions.

0:00 Welcome and ground rules. What is said here stays here unless the family agrees otherwise.
0:15 What matters. Each person reads or says, in their own words, what they want the family's wealth to make possible.
0:45 Values and vision refresh (Pillar 1). What has changed since last year, and what has not.
1:30 Break.
1:45 Decision rights and succession (Pillar 6). Who decides what today, who will decide it later, and how the next generation is being prepared.
2:15 Legacy and estate intentions (Pillar 7). The intentions behind the documents, explained by the family, with the attorney present if invited.
2:40 How we talk about money. One practice the family will keep this year.
2:55 Close. One commitment from each generation, and what goes into the Legacy Book this year.

After: recap within 24 hours to the parents; heirs receive only what the parents approve. Every commitment logged in Redtail.

materials.name: Next-Gen gathering outline
materials.note: Two hours, 10 to 15 adult heirs aged 18 to 30 from Tier 1 households, with parent consent. Education and peer connection, no sales content.
materials.body:
0:00 Arrivals and introductions: name, what you do, one money question you want answered tonight.
0:20 One topic the group chose in advance, 30 minutes, taught plainly.
0:50 Peer round: small tables, one prompt each. What did you learn about money growing up that you want to keep, and what do you want to do differently.
1:30 Open questions, answered in general terms only.
1:50 Close: how to reach Becky directly, and the date of next year's gathering.

Rules: no discussion of any family's plan; no photos or names shared without written consent; invitations cleared by compliance.

materials.name: Legacy Book outline
materials.when: Delivered at the third engagement anniversary
materials.note: Bound on archival paper. The family's own words and values only: no performance figures and no fee references.
materials.body:
1. The family, in its own words: who we are and where we come from.
2. What matters: the values statement from the Values, Vision and Purpose work.
3. The vision: what the family wants its wealth to make possible, across generations.
4. The company: how it was founded, the people who built it, and what it stands for.
5. How we decide: decision rights and how the family talks about money.
6. What each generation committed to, year by year, from the family sessions.
7. Letters: one page from each generation to the next, written by hand if they choose.
8. Blank pages for the next chapter.

milestones.budget: Proposed $750 per Tier 1 household a year, 2.9% of the modeled $25,500 gross revenue per family, or $15,000 across 20 families. Nothing is ordered until written gift and entertainment limits are in hand from the new broker-dealer.

catalog.gesture: Handwritten note plus a considered welcome gift
Personal year-end gift tied to the client's stated priorities

catalog.milestone: Business milestone: opening, new location, 10th or 25th anniversary, acquisition
Personal milestones: birth, grandchild, graduation, wedding, major anniversary, retirement
catalog.gesture: Note, call and a gesture; at most two a year

catalog.milestone: Key date card, milestone card, shared event seat

catalog.gesture: Call the same day, a note, and a hosted acknowledgment after close
catalog.ceiling: Inside the $200 personal line unless compliance sets otherwise

milestones.test: Would it still be on a shelf in 30 years. Durable, engraved to mark the event, personal to the family, and no firm logo. The firm appears only on a handwritten card.

heirlooms.milestone: Birth or adoption of a child or grandchild
heirlooms.item: Silver-plated piggy bank, engraved with the child's name and birth date
heirlooms.price: $59 to $79 at the retailers checked on November 9, 2026
heirlooms.note: Plated, not sterling. Never describe it as sterling.

heirlooms.item: Engraved frame holding a professional photo from the event
Engraved fountain pen or leather-bound journal
Engraved ribbon-cutting scissors plus a framed opening-day print
Bound founder's book: timeline, photos and the founder's own words
Engraved desk piece marking founding date to closing date
The Legacy Book, made with the family
heirlooms.note: Competes with the Roundtable seats for budget. Decide which is funded first.

engraving: Every gift is engraved to mark the event. Nothing leaves the office unengraved.
Text: the recipient or family name, the date and a short event line. For a business: the business name, the date and the occasion. Never the firm's name or logo.
Proof: Maddie checks spelling and dates against Redtail, and the client confirms the exact wording in writing before engraving.
Durability: record the engraving method and depth, the plating thickness, and whether the piece can be replated.
Acknowledge within 7 days by call or note. The object can follow within 21 days. If it cannot, tell the client the delivery date.
guardrails: Limits come from the broker-dealer's compliance manual. FINRA Rule 3220 is commonly cited as capping gifts at $100 per person per year in a business context. Verify the rule and the firm's limit in writing before any spend.
If a $100 annual aggregate applies to a recipient, gifts cannot stack. Move spend to hosted events, education and service, with compliance classifying each item.
Log every gift and event in Redtail with amount, date and recipient. Review totals per recipient each quarter.
No cash, no fee discounts, and nothing conditioned on a referral.
Client quotes, survey responses and endorsements need compliance clearance before any external use. The SEC Marketing Rule governs testimonials for advisory services.

occasions.name: Birthday
occasions.timing: Arrives on or before the day. Drafted 14 days ahead from the key date workflow.
cautions: Decade birthdays (40, 50, 60, 70, 80) for Tier 1 get a call as well as the card.
Verify the date in Redtail. A card on the wrong date is worse than no card.

occasions.name: Business anniversary (10th or 25th)
occasions.gift: Bound founder's book or engraved keepsake
cautions: A business anniversary is a relational touch, never a sales touch.

occasions.name: Grand opening or new location
occasions.timing: Becky attends in person where possible. Note within 7 days.
occasions.gift: Engraved ribbon-cutting scissors and a framed opening-day print

occasions.name: Birth or adoption of a child or grandchild
occasions.timing: Call or note within 7 days; the gift can follow within 21, because engraving adds time.
occasions.gift: Engraved baby rattle, brass or silver plated, with the first name and birth date (keep two in stock); or the engraved silver-plated piggy bank
occasions.ceiling: $200 line, at most two personal milestones a year
cautions: The card goes to the parents or grandparents, never to the child.
Record the birth date in Redtail only with the parent's consent.
Brass or silver plated. Never call silver plate sterling; sterling rattles usually run past the ceiling.
For a grandchild, send it to the grandparent to give, unless they ask otherwise.

occasions.name: Graduation
occasions.gift: Engraved fountain pen or leather-bound journal
cautions: If the graduate is an adult heir on the Next-Gen track, a note to them directly needs the parent's consent on file.

occasions.name: College acceptance, commitment or signing day
occasions.timing: Within 14 days of the news, and before move-in once the school is chosen.
occasions.gift: A hat or sweatshirt from the college, bought from the official campus store, sized through the parent
cautions: Ask the parent for the size quietly, or choose a hat.
Buy from the official store. Nothing with the firm's name on it.
For a grandchild, send it to the grandparent to give.
Wait until the choice is announced. An acceptance is not a decision.

occasions.name: A child's or grandchild's achievement
occasions.gift: A handwritten note addressed to the young person, sent to the parent or grandparent to pass on. Young people rarely get real mail.
cautions: Send it to the parent or grandparent to pass on, never directly to a minor.
Nothing about money, saving or the firm. It is a note to a young person, not a first touch.
Examples: Eagle Scout or Gold Award, a state title, all-state, honor society, valedictorian, a recital, a krewe court or a debut.

occasions.name: A grown child's first job, first home or first business
occasions.gift: A good book on the first years of earning, with an open invitation to a next-generation conversation, offered through the parent
cautions: The offer goes through the parent, and is made once.
Any conversation with an adult child follows the Next-Gen track, with the parent's consent on file.

occasions.name: Wedding or major anniversary
occasions.gift: Engraved frame for a photo from the day

occasions.name: Retirement
occasions.timing: Call the same week; note within 7 days.
occasions.gift: A gesture chosen from what they said they want to do next

occasions.name: Sale closing or exit
occasions.timing: Call the same day. Note within 7 days. Hosted acknowledgment after close.
occasions.gift: Engraved desk piece, founding date to closing date
occasions.ceiling: Inside the $200 line unless compliance sets otherwise

occasions.name: Engagement signed (welcome)
occasions.timing: Handwritten note on day 1 of the onboarding workflow.

occasions.name: December
occasions.timing: Delivered before the holidays. Year-end note to every Tier 1 household by December 18.
occasions.gift: A personal gift tied to what the client said matters this year

occasions.name: A loss in the family
occasions.timing: Becky calls within 1 business day. Handwritten note.
occasions.note:
Dear {{first}},

I am so sorry about {{name}}. I am thinking of you and your family.

There is nothing you need to do and nothing you need to answer. I am here whenever you want me.

With deepest sympathy,
{{advisorFirst}}
cautions: No gift, no marketing, and no business conversation unless the client raises it.
Apply the Life Event tag. No referral ask while it is open.

occasions.name: Thank you for an introduction
occasions.timing: Handwritten within 24 hours of the introduction, whether or not it converts.
occasions.ceiling: No gift tied to a referral
cautions: Never include anything about the prospect beyond what the prospect has allowed.
Nothing of value is offered for an introduction without the broker-dealer's written approval.

templates.body:
Never in the same conversation as an open problem, and never during a Life Event.

"I am glad this has been useful. The owners I do my best work for usually come from people like you. Is there one person you think of who is carrying a business and a family plan that have never been put on the same page. If you are comfortable, I would welcome an introduction. It would be a 45-minute conversation with me, no obligation, and I will not contact anyone else in your circle."

eventRules: Tier 1: a personal call first, then the written invitation 30 days before. Tiers 2 and 3: the written invitation 30 days before.
Tag each event in Redtail (for example, Event: Roundtable 2027-03) and track RSVPs on the household.
Reminder 7 days before. Dietary preferences are captured for logistics only.
Follow-up call or note within 48 hours. Log what the client raised and any introductions offered.
Cost per attendee is logged against the gift and entertainment limits.
Invitations, speaker content and programs route through broker-dealer compliance before use.
No photos or client names are posted or shown without written consent and compliance clearance. Roundtable attendees are never named outside the room.
No reference to any prior affiliation in any event material. The community name stays a working label until trademark counsel and compliance clear one.

guardrails: Every consumer-facing template, invitation and printed piece routes through broker-dealer compliance before use, and only the new firm's disclosures appear.
No reference to any prior affiliation in footers, templates, signature blocks or event materials.
No contractions in client or COI correspondence, invitations, letters or the Legacy Book. Exact figures with a named source. No manufactured urgency.
Client names, quotes and photographs appear in nothing external without written consent and compliance clearance.
Nothing about Contnuum appears in any client piece, and no client data flows to it.
Maddie never gives advice or answers a planning question in writing, and never contacts a client's CPA or attorney without Becky's instruction and the client's authorization.
No email goes out in response to a distressed or angry message without Becky reading it first.
